These are registered domestic moves between municipalities, not unique people. A person can move more than once. The data shows where and when moves happen, but cannot tell us why someone moved.

SOURCES & METHODS

A map you can check.

This independent atlas uses Statistics Denmark’s open StatBank data. It is not an official Statistics Denmark product.

What is counted?

FLY66 records domestic moves from one municipality to another, by year, single year of age and recorded sex. We include all published years, 2006–2025, all 98 municipalities and Christiansø. Eight non-overlapping age bands cover ages 0–125. “Everyone” sums the source’s men and women categories.

A move is an event, not a unique person. Moves within a municipality, international migration, births and deaths are excluded. Net domestic moves therefore do not equal total population growth. The 2006 source figures were restated to the municipality structure introduced in 2007.

What does “per 1,000” mean?

Net moves divided by the population at 1 January of the same year, age group and sex, multiplied by 1,000. Population comes from FOLK1A, available here from 2008. Rates are unavailable for 2006–2007. This is not the probability that an individual moves; people age and can move repeatedly during a year. Small populations can produce large rates.

How are connected groups found?

For the selected year, age and sex, each municipality is a node. The weight between two places is the sum of moves in both directions. NetworkX’s Louvain algorithm groups places with relatively dense exchanges (resolution 1, fixed seed 42). These are exploratory groups, not official regions or commuting zones. Group membership can change with the filters; colours do not identify the same group across years.

What is checked?

Single-age records are grouped without overlap; missing values are rejected, and omitted BULK combinations count as zero under the source API’s documented rules. Every Copenhagen-origin route is independently checked against source-calculated all-age totals, for both sexes and every year. Arrivals and departures reconcile nationally; age-band population totals reconcile to the source totals. Read the validation record ↗

Sources, dates & reuse

Statistical data: © Statistics Denmark, CC BY 4.0. Map: Eurostat GISCO LAU 2024, simplified for display. © EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries. The geometry has separate non-commercial use terms. It is a fixed reference map, not a reconstruction of each year’s boundaries.

Age comparisons describe different groups in the same year. They do not follow a cohort or demonstrate causes such as housing prices, education or employment.
